name: Charge pump · inverter, chip (TC1044S)
description: A TC1044S wired as a voltage inverter (Microchip TC1044S data sheet (DS21348A), Figure 3): about −V+ (−9 V from 9 V, less 60 Ω × the current drawn) on its own net VNEG, for a ± supply. Label the stages it powers VNEG (an op-amp's negative supply, say). C1 is the reservoir (10 µF, as the datasheet's), its + side to ground. C2 is the flying cap, pin 2 (+) to pin 4 (D-226). Boost is on (about 22 kHz pump).

notes.part:U1: Inverter: V+ in, about −V+ out. Supply: pin 8 is the chip's supply input, fed from the pedal's V+ (the DC jack or the battery, through the input filter). The pump draws its current in short pulses at its switching rate; a bulk electrolytic on V+ (10-100 µF, such as the Input filter block's 47 Ω and 100 µF) supplies them close by, so they don't travel back along V+ and whine in the other stages. A pedal that already has one on V+ needs no second cap here (one close to pin 8 helps a little on a long board). A pedal with none, such as a bare battery fuzz like the Rangemaster, needs one: the "Supply without a bulk capacitor" warning says so.
notes.part:C1: Reservoir, + to ground: VNEG is below ground.
notes.net:VNEG: About −9 V from a 9 V supply, less 60 Ω × the current drawn.
notes.part:C2: Flying cap: charged from V+, then flipped onto VNEG every cycle. + to pin 2.
